records.topic: CO object that holds cost before settlement
records.claim_text: In SAP, the account assignment object for purchase orders and actual postings on an investment measure is always the internal order or the WBS element, never the asset under construction.
records.evidence_quote: The account assignment object for purchase orders and actual posting is always the order or the WBS element.

records.topic: Investment measure is not its own object type
records.claim_text: An investment measure is not a distinct object type in SAP and has no master record of its own.
records.evidence_quote: Measures are not an object type in their own right in the SAP System, meaning they do not have their own master record.

records.claim_text: An investment measure is represented by either an internal order master record or a WBS element of a project.
records.evidence_quote: They are represented in the system using special master records of one of the following: Internal orders, WBS elements of a project.

records.topic: Role of the AuC in the balance sheet
records.claim_text: The asset under construction is the mechanism that carries the capitalised portion of an investment measure onto the balance sheet general ledger accounts.
records.evidence_quote: The asset under construction is the vehicle for the balance sheet transfer to the corresponding general ledger account(s).

records.claim_text: Project networks cannot themselves be investment measures because they cannot be linked to an asset under construction; they must be settled to a WBS element first.
records.evidence_quote: Project networks cannot be represented directly as investment measures, since they cannot be linked to assets under construction.

records.topic: Investment profile makes an object an investment measure
records.claim_text: Assigning an investment profile to an order or WBS element is what turns that object into an investment measure.
records.evidence_quote: By assigning an investment profile to an order or WBS element, you make it into an investment measure.

records.topic: Investment profile controls automatic AuC creation
records.claim_text: The investment profile specifies automatic creation of an accompanying asset under construction at the moment the order or WBS element is released.
records.evidence_quote: You make the following specifications in the investment profile: Automatic creation of an accompanying asset under construction when the order or WBS element is released.

records.claim_text: The investment profile's Fixed default class indicator decides whether the proposed AuC asset class may be changed by the user.
records.evidence_quote: Using the Fixed default class indicator, you specify whether this is a default value that can be changed or not.

records.claim_text: Line item settlement allows a separate settlement rule to be created for each individual debit posted to the investment measure.
records.evidence_quote: Line item settlement has the following advantages: You can create settlement rules for individual line items (debits).

records.claim_text: SAP documents that the benefits of line item settlement are traded against reduced system performance.
records.evidence_quote: The advantages of line item settlement, however, are offset by reductions in performance.

records.claim_text: An order or WBS element can be made an investment measure after creation, but only if it has not yet been settled.
records.evidence_quote: However, this procedure is only possible if the order or WBS element has not yet been settled.

records.topic: Release triggers the investment profile check
records.claim_text: On release of the order or WBS element the system checks whether an investment profile is assigned, which is the trigger for AuC creation.
records.evidence_quote: When the order or WBS element is released, the system checks whether an investment profile has been assigned to it.

records.claim_text: After the AuC is generated the investment measure receives a system status recording that an asset under construction was created.
records.evidence_quote: The system then assigns the investment measure Asset under construction created system status.

records.topic: AuC asset class must use internal numbering
records.claim_text: Asset classes used for automatically created assets under construction must use internal number assignment.
records.evidence_quote: Number assignment must be internal when you plan to use the automatic creation of an asset under construction

records.topic: AuC master data inherited from the CO object
records.claim_text: The automatically created AuC inherits its description and organisational assignments directly from the order or WBS element.
records.evidence_quote: The system copies the description and the organizational assignments directly from the order or WBS element.

records.claim_text: One investment measure can carry more than one asset under construction.
records.evidence_quote: It is possible for an investment measure to have more than one asset under construction.

records.claim_text: An investment measure can hold one asset under construction for each source assignment defined in its source structure.
records.evidence_quote: It can have an asset under construction for each source assignment in the source structure used.

records.topic: Capitalisation key defined at company code level
records.claim_text: Capitalisation keys, which control what percentage of a cost element is capitalised, are defined at company code level.
records.evidence_quote: You define capitalization keys at company code level.

records.claim_text: The percentage of each cost element or activity type that may be capitalised is specified in a capitalisation key.
records.evidence_quote: You specify the percentages to be capitalized in a capitalization key.

records.claim_text: Costs that do not require capitalisation are posted by the system to a non-operating expense account.
records.evidence_quote: The system posts costs which do not require capitalization to the account for nonoperating expense.

records.claim_text: The account used for non-capitalisable amounts during settlement cannot be a cost element.
records.evidence_quote: The account cannot be a cost element.

records.topic: Two settlement modes for investment measures
records.claim_text: SAP settles investment measures in two modes: periodic settlement at period close and full settlement or partial capitalisation at completion.
records.evidence_quote: There are two ways of settling investment measures: Periodic settlement at the close of the period

records.claim_text: Full settlement is performed when the investment measure is completed.
records.evidence_quote: Full settlement takes place when the investment measure is completed.

records.claim_text: Full settlement transfers the debits previously capitalised on the asset under construction onto the completed fixed assets.
records.evidence_quote: During the full settlement, the debits that were transferred to the asset under construction are settled to completed assets.

records.claim_text: Acquisitions can still be posted to an investment measure after a full settlement has been carried out.
records.evidence_quote: You can still post acquisitions to the investment measure after the full settlement.

records.claim_text: There is no limit to the number of full settlements that can be executed for the same investment measure.
records.evidence_quote: It is possible to have any number of full settlements for the same investment measure.

records.claim_text: Settlement to the asset under construction can be defined separately for each depreciation area.
records.evidence_quote: You can define the settlement to assets under construction for each depreciation area.

records.topic: Technically completed status gates full settlement
records.claim_text: Full settlement is executed once the investment measure carries technically completed status.
records.evidence_quote: As soon as an investment measure has technically completed status, the system carries out full settlement.

records.claim_text: Settlement rules must exist on the investment measure before a full settlement can be posted.
records.evidence_quote: Before you post the full settlement, you have to create settlement rules for the investment measure.

records.claim_text: Creating the receiving asset from the order or WBS element master data makes the system generate a full settlement rule with equivalence number 1 and that asset as receiver.
records.evidence_quote: The system then automatically creates a full settlement rule with equivalence number 1 and the newly created asset as the receiver.

records.claim_text: Once a settlement has been posted, the distribution rules that were used can no longer be changed.
records.evidence_quote: After the settlement is posted, the distribution rules used can no longer be changed.

records.topic: Adding receivers for the open amount
records.claim_text: New receivers may be added for the portion of the investment measure that remains unsettled after a partial capitalisation.
records.evidence_quote: However, you can add new receivers for the amount that is still open.

records.topic: Only current-year debits settle to CO receivers
records.claim_text: Only debits posted in the current fiscal year may be settled to CO receivers such as cost centres.
records.evidence_quote: It is a fundamental rule that only debits from the current fiscal year can be settled to CO receivers.

records.claim_text: Partial capitalisation exists because different parts of a large investment measure are frequently put into service one after another.
records.evidence_quote: Especially when you have a large capital investment measure, you may put different parts of it into service, one after the other.

records.topic: Validity period on partial capitalisation rules
records.claim_text: Settlement rules used for partial capitalisation must carry the period from which the rule becomes valid.
records.evidence_quote: In the settlement rules for partial capitalization, you have to enter the period in which the rule becomes valid

records.claim_text: Settlement rules are stored in the master record of the internal order or WBS element, not on the asset.
records.evidence_quote: You enter the settlement rules in the master record of the order or WBS element.

records.topic: Summary vs line item settlement switch
records.claim_text: Whether settlement is summary or by line item is a setting in the investment profile.
records.evidence_quote: In the investment profile you specify whether settlement is summary settlement or by line item.

records.claim_text: A settlement rule can distribute by percentage rate, by equivalence number, or by a directly entered amount.
records.evidence_quote: Along with the option of settling on the basis of percentage rates or equivalence numbers, it is also possible to enter specific amounts directly.

records.claim_text: If no capitalisation key is maintained, periodic settlement moves 100 percent of the debits to the asset under construction.
records.evidence_quote: If you do not enter any capitalization keys, the system settles all debits to the asset under construction during periodic settlement.

records.claim_text: A distribution rule states the settlement receiver, the share of costs settled to it, and when the settlement occurs.
records.evidence_quote: Which settlement receiver you settle to, which part of the costs you settle, when you make the settlement.

records.topic: Percentage or equivalence number on the distribution rule
records.claim_text: The share of cost carried by a distribution rule is expressed either as a percentage rate or as an equivalence number.
records.evidence_quote: You can specify percentage rates or equivalence numbers.

records.claim_text: A settlement rule defines what proportion of the costs on a sender object is settled to which receivers.
records.evidence_quote: Defines what proportion of the costs on a sender should be settled to which receiver(s).

records.claim_text: The system assigns the asset under construction to the investment measure automatically when the investment measure is released.
records.evidence_quote: The system automatically assigns the asset under construction to the investment measure when the investment measure is released

records.claim_text: Periodic settlement to CO receivers uses settlement type PRE on the settlement rule.
records.evidence_quote: Settlement rule for the periodic settlement to CO receivers (settlement type PRE)

records.claim_text: The settlement rule for the completion of an investment measure uses settlement type FUL.
records.evidence_quote: Settlement rule for the full settlement when the investment measure is complete (settlement type FUL)

records.claim_text: Line item settlement operates through distribution rule groups that are assigned to one or more line items of the investment measure.
records.evidence_quote: You can assign these distribution rule groups to one or more line items in an investment measure

records.topic: Allowed receivers controlled by settlement profile
records.claim_text: The settlement profile determines which receiver types are permitted for settlement.
records.evidence_quote: The allowed receivers are specified in the settlement profile

records.claim_text: The settlement profile holds the principal control indicators for settlement plus default values for the allocation structure and source structure.
records.evidence_quote: The settlement profile also contains default values for the allocation structure and for the source structure.

records.topic: Settlement cost element in the allocation structure
records.claim_text: The cost element used for periodic settlement to an AuC or to CO receivers is specified in the allocation structure of the settlement profile.
records.evidence_quote: You specify the cost element for the periodic settlement to an asset under construction or to CO receivers

records.topic: Secondary costs need a settlement cost element
records.claim_text: Secondary cost elements cannot be settled by cost element and must be settled using a settlement cost element.
records.evidence_quote: You have to settle secondary cost elements using a settlement cost element.

records.topic: Full settlement needs no cost element
records.claim_text: Full settlement requires no cost element because it is only a transfer posting from the AuC to completed assets.
records.evidence_quote: You do not need cost elements for the full settlement, since this is just a transfer posting from assets under construction to completed assets.

records.claim_text: Activity allocation and overhead can both be charged to investment projects and internal orders.
records.evidence_quote: You can charge activity allocation, as well as overhead, to projects and internal orders.

records.claim_text: Overhead on an order or project is calculated from a costing sheet key supplied on the object.
records.evidence_quote: In order to calculate overhead on an order or project, you have to supply the key of the costing sheet.

records.topic: No direct posting to the AuC
records.claim_text: Costs cannot be posted directly to the asset under construction belonging to an investment measure; they must be posted to the CO object.
records.evidence_quote: You cannot post directly to the asset under construction that belongs to the investment measure.

records.claim_text: Periodic settlement splits the accumulated costs into capitalisable and non-capitalisable amounts.
records.evidence_quote: During the periodic settlement, the costs are divided into amounts requiring capitalization and those not requiring capitalization

records.claim_text: Periodic settlement credits the CO object and reclassifies the capitalisable amounts from expense to assets.
records.evidence_quote: The periodic settlement credits the order or WBS element and transfers the amounts requiring capitalization from costs (expense) to assets

records.topic: Purpose of periodic settlement to CO receivers
records.claim_text: Periodic settlement to CO receivers exists so debits never intended for capitalisation can be moved straight to cost centres.
records.evidence_quote: Periodic settlement to CO receivers makes it possible to post debits to the investment measure which are not intended for later capitalization.

records.claim_text: Settling selected line items to CO receivers is used where incidental non-capitalisable costs have been posted to the investment measure.
records.evidence_quote: The settlement of certain line items to CO receivers is especially useful when certain incidental costs have been posted to an investment measure.

records.claim_text: The capitalised balance of one asset under construction can be settled to several different completed assets.
records.evidence_quote: It is settled to three different assets.

records.claim_text: In the documented value-flow example the residual amount that fails the capitalisation test is posted to non-operating expense.
records.evidence_quote: The remaining 1000 goes to nonoperating expense.

records.claim_text: A fixed asset receiver on a settlement rule is entered with receiver type FXA.
records.evidence_quote: Enter receiver type FXA (= fixed asset).

records.claim_text: Additional receiving assets are entered on the full settlement rule with a percentage rate or equivalence number and settlement type FUL.
records.evidence_quote: Enter additional receiving assets, the percentage rate (or equivalence number) and settlement type FUL.

records.topic: Write-off of abandoned investment at full settlement
records.claim_text: At full settlement amounts previously held on the AuC but later judged non-capitalisable can be corrected out to CO receivers as expense.
records.evidence_quote: This can be useful, for instance, for 'dry hole costs,' that is, amounts were assigned to assets under construction but later are registered as expense.

records.topic: Fiscal-year limit on write-off to CO
records.claim_text: The correction of AuC amounts to CO receivers at full settlement is restricted to costs of the current fiscal year.
records.evidence_quote: However, this only applies to costs in the current fiscal year, not for prior years.

records.claim_text: A settlement run is executed for a WBS element or order with period, fiscal year and a processing type, where processing type 1 is automatic.
records.evidence_quote: Enter the WBS element or order, the period, the fiscal year, and the processing type (1 = automatic).

records.claim_text: The value date used for a settlement posting is entered on the initial screen of the settlement transaction.
records.evidence_quote: You can enter the value date for the settlement in the initial screen of the settlement transaction.

records.claim_text: SAP prescribes performing a periodic settlement at the close of every cost accounting period.
records.evidence_quote: You should carry out a periodic settlement at the close of each cost accounting period.

records.topic: Down payment balance condition for full settlement
records.claim_text: At full settlement the down payments and their clearings must net to zero.
records.evidence_quote: At the time of the full settlement, the down payments and the down payment clearings to be settled have to balance to zero.

records.claim_text: Only the most recently performed settlement can be reversed.
records.evidence_quote: You can only reverse the most recently performed settlement.

records.claim_text: The move of a self-constructed asset from the under-construction phase to the useful-life phase is termed capitalisation of the asset under construction.
records.evidence_quote: The transition between these two phases is called 'capitalization of the asset under construction.'

records.claim_text: An asset under construction is either a normal asset master record or a master record with line item management.
records.evidence_quote: The asset under construction can be either a normal asset record, or a master record with line item management.

records.topic: Capitalisable portion must go to capitalised assets
records.claim_text: The portion of an AuC that requires capitalisation must be settled to capitalised fixed assets.
records.evidence_quote: You must settle those parts of the asset under construction that require capitalization to capitalized assets.

records.claim_text: Any down payments must be reversed before a full transfer of the asset under construction can be carried out.
records.evidence_quote: Before carrying out a full transfer of an asset under construction, you have to reverse any down payments.

records.claim_text: Ordinary depreciation is not permitted on assets under construction in most countries.
records.evidence_quote: Ordinary depreciation is not allowed for assets under construction in most countries.

records.claim_text: Assets under construction are normally shown as their own balance sheet item.
records.evidence_quote: They are usually displayed as a separate balance sheet item.

records.claim_text: Several assets under construction may be managed collectively on a single master record.
records.evidence_quote: You can also use collective management of several assets under construction on one master record.

records.topic: Line item settlement receivers may be G/L accounts
records.claim_text: In AuC line item settlement the distribution rule receivers may be assets or general ledger accounts, distributed by percentage or equivalence number.
records.evidence_quote: Enter the means for the distribution in the settlement distribution rule (percentage rates or equivalence numbers) and the respective receivers (assets or general ledger accounts).

records.topic: Automatic deactivation of a fully settled AuC
records.claim_text: When an AuC has been settled to zero in all depreciation areas the system deactivates it automatically.
records.evidence_quote: the system automatically deactivates the asset under construction

records.topic: Asset value date derived from capitalisation date
records.claim_text: For the AuC-to-asset transfer transaction types the asset value date is derived from the capitalisation date of the completed asset.
records.evidence_quote: The asset value date for the transfer is determined for these transaction types by the capitalization date of the completed asset.

records.claim_text: AuC capitalisation uses transaction type 348 for prior-year acquisitions and 349 for current-year acquisitions.
records.evidence_quote: Use the appropriate transaction type (348 for prior-year acquisitions, 349 for current-year acquisitions).

records.topic: Depreciation area restriction during full settlement
records.claim_text: During full settlement the transaction type cannot be limited to specific depreciation areas of the capitalised asset.
records.evidence_quote: Limiting the transaction type to specific depreciation areas of the capitalized asset is not possible during full settlement.

records.claim_text: The asset value date is the value date of an asset transaction seen from the asset accounting perspective.
records.evidence_quote: The asset value date is the value date of an asset transaction from the asset accounting point of view.

records.claim_text: The capitalisation date can be entered manually when the asset master record is created.
records.evidence_quote: You can enter the capitalization date manually when you create the asset master record.

records.topic: Capitalisation date defaults the asset value date
records.claim_text: A manually entered capitalisation date becomes the default asset value date of the first acquisition posted to that asset.
records.evidence_quote: The system uses this date as the default asset value date when you post the first acquisition to the asset.

records.claim_text: If no capitalisation date is maintained, the system adopts the asset value date of the first capitalising posting.
records.evidence_quote: If you do not enter a capitalization date in the asset master record, the system automatically adopts the asset value date.

records.topic: Asset value date drives depreciation start
records.claim_text: The asset value date, adjusted by the depreciation key's period control, determines the depreciation start date.
records.evidence_quote: The asset value date, corrected by the period control of the depreciation key, is the key factor in determining the depreciation start date.

records.claim_text: Setting the Closed status on a WBS element deactivates the assets under construction assigned to it.
records.evidence_quote: The status deactivates assets in construction that are assigned to the WBS element.

records.claim_text: Removing an asset from the portfolio with no revenue, for example by scrapping, is a retirement without revenue.
records.evidence_quote: A retirement without revenue is the removal of an asset from the asset portfolio without any revenue, for example, by scrapping.

records.claim_text: A retirement may cover an entire fixed asset or only part of it.
records.evidence_quote: An asset retirement can refer to an entire fixed asset (complete retirement) or part of a fixed asset (partial retirement).

records.topic: Investment order creates AuC on release
records.claim_text: For an investment order the system usually creates the asset under construction automatically when the order is released.
records.evidence_quote: The system usually creates an asset under construction automatically when the investment order is released.

records.claim_text: Flagging an investment order for deletion automatically deactivates its asset under construction.
records.evidence_quote: When you flag an investment order for deletion, the AuC is automatically deactivated.

records.topic: Networks settle up to the WBS element first
records.claim_text: Networks assigned to an investment WBS element must first be settled to that WBS element before it can be settled onward.
records.evidence_quote: You first have to settle all networks assigned to the WBS element to that WBS element (multiple settlement).

records.claim_text: The periodic settlement of a higher WBS element can only be posted after all subordinate objects have been settled by cost element to it.
records.evidence_quote: can only be posted after all the subordinate objects are settled by cost element to the investment measure

records.claim_text: Some jurisdictions require interest to be calculated on capital invested in an asset under construction.
records.evidence_quote: In certain countries, you are required to calculate interest on capital invested in an asset under construction.

records.claim_text: Interest during construction can only be calculated for investment measures managed as projects, not as orders.
records.evidence_quote: You can only calculate interest for investment measures that are managed as projects (not orders).

records.claim_text: Interest is not calculated on amounts that were settled as costs to CO receivers.
records.evidence_quote: Interest is not calculated on amounts that were settled as costs to CO receivers.

records.claim_text: A line-item proof of origin from the completed asset back to the original debit is only possible with line item settlement.
records.evidence_quote: Note that you can only generate a line-item proof of origin if you use line item (not summary) settlement.

records.topic: Distribution rule group on the AuC
records.claim_text: Several asset-specific distribution rules together form a distribution rule group on the asset under construction.
records.evidence_quote: Several distribution rules form a distribution rule group

records.claim_text: The distribution key on an AuC distribution rule is either an equivalence number or a percentage rate.
records.evidence_quote: The distribution key can be equivalence numbers or percentage rates

records.topic: AuC assignment to WBS element in Project System
records.claim_text: An asset under construction can be assigned to a WBS element for capital investment measures.
records.evidence_quote: You can assign an asset under construction to a WBS element for capital investment measures.

records.claim_text: Down payments made for investment measures count as acquisition postings.
records.evidence_quote: Down payments made for investment measures represent acquisition postings.

records.topic: Down payments must be assigned to the WBS element
records.claim_text: Down payments cannot be transferred from a network to a WBS element, so they must be account-assigned directly to the WBS element.
records.evidence_quote: Down payments cannot be transferred from a network to a WBS element.

records.claim_text: Down payments on fixed assets generally have to be capitalised and reported in a separate balance sheet item.
records.evidence_quote: Down payments represent a type of acquisition to fixed assets which you generally need to capitalize and report in a separate balance sheet item.

records.topic: Legacy transfer of prior-year AuC line items
records.claim_text: AuC line items acquired in previous fiscal years must be migrated with the special legacy transaction types 900 and 910.
records.evidence_quote: Line items that were acquired in previous fiscal years have to be transferred using the special transaction types for legacy data (900, 910).

records.topic: Historical asset value date not migratable
records.claim_text: The historical asset value date cannot be carried over for prior-year AuC line items during legacy data transfer.
records.evidence_quote: You cannot transfer the historical asset value date for these transactions.

records.claim_text: Each settlement share of a blanket rule carries receiver type, receiver, percentage or equivalence number, settlement type and source assignment.
records.evidence_quote: For each settlement share, enter the receiver type (such as CTR for cost center)

records.topic: Settlement type codes PRE and FUL
records.claim_text: The settlement type field takes PRE for preliminary settlement and FUL for full settlement.
records.evidence_quote: Settlement type (PRE = preliminary settlement or FUL = full settlement)

records.topic: Source structure splits cost by cost element range
records.claim_text: A source structure lets one cost element range be settled on a different distribution than another within the same measure.
records.evidence_quote: For cost elements 100 to 200, the system settles 60% to cost center 5036 and 40% to cost center 5037.

records.claim_text: For line item settlement the user selects line items and enters the receiver plus the percentage rate or equivalence number.
records.evidence_quote: Enter the receiving cost centers (or other receivers) and the percentage rate (or equivalence number) for the settlement.

records.claim_text: Investment Management integrates with Asset Accounting to capitalise the capitalisable costs of internal orders and WBS elements to a fixed asset.
records.evidence_quote: enables you to easily capitalize the costs of internal orders and WBS elements that require capitalization to a fixed asset

records.claim_text: In S/4HANA the AuC master record is generated by assigning an investment profile to the project or WBS element and releasing it.
records.evidence_quote: The AuC Master Record is generated by assigning an investment profile to the project or WBS element and releasing the corresponding element.

records.claim_text: An asset under construction is not depreciated; only the completed operational asset is.
records.evidence_quote: An AuC is not depreciated. Only the completed operational asset is depreciated.

records.claim_text: Depreciation key 0000 is used so that no depreciation is calculated for the asset under construction in any depreciation area.
records.evidence_quote: The standard depreciation key 0000 ensures that in depreciation areas, no depreciation is calculated for AuC.

records.topic: One AuC can yield several assets
records.claim_text: One or more completed assets can arise from a single AuC, and those receiving assets are stored in the settlement rule.
records.evidence_quote: One or more assets can arise from an AuC. These assets are stored in the settlement rule.

records.topic: Default when no settlement rule exists
records.claim_text: Without an explicit settlement rule everything on the investment project is settled automatically to the assigned AuC.
records.evidence_quote: If a settlement rule is not set, everything is automatically settled to the assigned AuC.

records.topic: No investment profile means no AuC
records.claim_text: If a WBS element carries no investment profile, no asset under construction is created for it.
records.evidence_quote: If a WBS element is not linked to an investment profile, no AuC is created.

records.topic: Full settlement rule must total 100 percent
records.claim_text: The settlement rule used for full settlement must add up to 100 percent in total.
records.evidence_quote: The settlement rule must settle 100% in total.

records.topic: Prior-year debits cannot be expensed at closure
records.claim_text: Debits from previous fiscal years cannot be corrected to cost centres at full settlement because they already sat in the prior-year balance sheet.
records.evidence_quote: Debits from previous fiscal years cannot be settled to cost centers at this point

records.topic: Periodic settlement default is 100 percent to AuC
records.claim_text: By default the periodic settlement moves 100 percent of the WBS element costs to the AuC it is linked to.
records.evidence_quote: 100% of the costs are automatically settled to the AuC to which the WBS element is linked

records.topic: Event-based settlement removes the periodic run
records.claim_text: With event-based settlement there are no periodic settlements to the asset under construction.
records.evidence_quote: During event-based settlement, there are no periodic settlements to an asset under construction.

records.topic: Event-based settlement posts straight to AuC
records.claim_text: Under event-based settlement all costs of the investment project post directly and completely to the asset under construction.
records.evidence_quote: All costs of the investment project are posted completely directly to the asset under construction.

records.claim_text: With event-based settlement, settlement rules apply to all line items of the AuC and cannot be assigned per line item.
records.evidence_quote: It is not possible to assign settlement rules on line-item level.

The nearest documented SAP construct is periodic settlement of non-capitalisable incidental costs to CO receivers, and the 'dry hole costs' correction at full settlement. Any pre-operative-expense requirement must be modelled on those two mechanisms, not on a native SAP feature of that name.

INVESTMENT PROFILE FIELD LIST: no first-party SAP page enumerating every OITA field (Manage AuC, Investment measure asset class, Fixed default class, AuC per source structure, Settlement summary vs line item) was reachable. COMPONENTISATION: SAP has no object literally called a 'component'. Evidence supports (a) multiple AuC per measure via source structure, (b) one AuC settling to several completed assets with percentage or equivalence shares, (c) asset sub-numbers via partial retirement/transfer. There is no single first-party page describing componentisation as a named process.

ABANDONED / CANCELLED PROJECT WRITE-OFF: SAP documents two partial mechanisms - correction of current-fiscal-year AuC debits to CO receivers at full settlement ('dry hole costs'), and FI-AA asset retirement without revenue (scrapping) producing a loss equal to net book value. No first-party page was found that describes an end-to-end 'cancel the investment project and write off the CWIP' procedure; the design must compose the two.
